1921.readme:
sfzoning.com: San Francisco historic zoning (1921, sheets)

WHAT THIS FILE IS
The aligned sheets of the 1921 edition zoning map, one GeoTIFF per sheet, each
at its own resolution (California State Plane III, feet, EPSG:2227). Each
sheet was warped onto that grid with GDAL (gdalwarp, thin plate spline, cubic
resampling) from control points matched to today's street corners. Sheets
scanned in 1-bit black and white are tinted to the paper colour, and printed
border rules and binding shadows are erased. Nothing is vectorized or drawn on
the scans.

HOW THE ZONING WAS ASSIGNED
The zoning maps were read from the scans, one district label per area, and
each label was assigned to today's lots. The boundaries in the lot and
district files are modern lot lines from the DataSF parcels layer. They were
never traced from the scan, so a district edge is only as precise as the lot
it falls on. Where a street has moved since the map was drawn, the scan keeps
the historic position and the data follows today's lot lines.

WHAT "confidence" MEANS
A number from 0 to 1 for how sure the reading is that the lot belongs to the
district shown. Lots set by a person get 1: those whose district was set by an
override (inputs/<series>/overrides.csv in the source repository), and those
whose label a person added by hand (inputs/<series>/label_fixes.csv). Lots
read from a sheet flagged for review are capped at 0.6. 0 means no district
could be assigned to the lot.

NOT AN OFFICIAL RECORD
This is a reconstruction, not an official record of the San Francisco
Planning Department. Check the Planning Department's own records before
relying on it for any legal purpose.
